subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the volume of the parallelepiped whose coterminous edges are the vectors 2i − 3j + 2k, i − j + 2k and 2i + j − k.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.72, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 22. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives half the marks to the determinant and a full mark to the modulus, because a negative triple product reported as a volume is the single most common loss here. Three evaluations agree at −11: the first-row expansion gives 2(1 − 2) + 3(−1 − 4) + 2(1 + 2) = −11; the third-row expansion gives 2(−4) − 2 − 1 = −11; and computing b × c = (−1, 5, 3) and dotting with a gives −2 − 15 + 6 = −11. The volume is therefore |−11| = 11 cubic units, never −11. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this volume — the formula, the determinant, and what you do with the sign.

steps.label: State the formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. Coterminous means the three edges already meet at one corner, so no subtraction is needed.
steps.memory_tip: Parallelepiped is the whole box product; the tetrahedron gets one sixth of it.

recall.must_convey: That the volume of a parallelepiped on coterminous edges is the modulus of their box product.
accept: the volume is mod of the box product of the three edges
coterminous edges go straight in with no subtraction
V equals mod a b c
coterminous ante oke corner daggara kalise edges

steps.why: The three edges meet at one corner, so they go straight into the box product with no subtraction, and the modulus is what makes the answer a volume.
common_mistakes: Using ⅙|[a b c]|, which is the tetrahedron formula.
Subtracting the vectors first; these are already edges, not corners.

steps.label: Evaluate the determinant
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Rows are the three edges in the order given. Watch the minus in front of the middle term.
steps.memory_tip: The middle cofactor carries a minus, so −(−3) becomes +3 in front of its bracket.

recall.must_convey: That the determinant of the three edges is −11.
accept: expand the three by three determinant to get minus eleven
b cross c is minus one, five, three and dotting with a gives minus eleven
the box product is minus eleven
determinant expand cheste minus eleven vasthundi

steps.why: Computing b × c first and dotting with a is the definition of the box product, so it must agree with the determinant.
common_mistakes: Getting the sign of the middle cofactor wrong.

steps.label: Take the modulus
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The negative sign is about the order of the edges, not the size of the box.
steps.memory_tip: The sign belongs to the ORDER of the edges; the size is always the modulus.
lines: A volume is never negative, so take
the modulus of the box product.

recall.must_convey: That the volume is |−11| = 11 cubic units.
accept: take the modulus so the volume is eleven cubic units
a volume cannot be negative, so eleven
modulus teeskunte eleven cubic units vasthundi
the minus sign only records the order of the edges

steps.why: A negative triple product only means the three edges were taken in the left-handed order; the box itself still holds 11 cubic units.
common_mistakes: Writing square units instead of cubic units.
